lines.tagline: The late bloomer: a drifting wisp for most of the road, then a sun or a moon at the end of it.

potent_at.why: The late one. Its only attack before the first badge is Swift (Normal, resisted by Brock's Rock types); Confusion comes at 21 and the Psychic and Steel moves through the 30s, so Cosmog trails the field until 45. Then the native final (680 BST) carries Sabrina and Blaine: Lunala's Moongeist Beam and Psychic, or Solgaleo's Sunsteel Strike.

lines.tagline: Fast out of the gate, then two scrolls and one choice: which kind of fighter it becomes.

potent_at.why: The early one. Fighting moves arrive first (Low Sweep 6, Rock Tomb 14), so it leads Brock (Rock) and stays level-best through Misty and Surge, where Brick Break and Dig (26, 28) answer Magneton and the Electric types; after 30 it gains little until Urshifu at 45. Its scrolls are the station's to give.

lines.tagline: The closer: plain and patient through the middle of the journey, then any type it remembers, its memories earned in the story.

potent_at.why: The closer. A Normal-type with even stats and only Normal, Fang and Zen Headbutt coverage before 42, it is the weakest of the five through the midgame; Surf (42) and Ice Beam (44), carried into Silvally, sweep Giovanni's Ground team.

lines.tagline: A small poison with a sharp midgame, grown into a dragon that gets stronger with every knockout.

potent_at.why: The midgame one. Poison attacks from the start (Venoshock 6, Poison Jab 16) are resisted by Brock but super effective into Erika (Grass) and resisted by her team in return, so it sweeps gym 4 alone. Sludge Bomb waits until 36 so the Erika spike is the stage-2 form's, not a stronger move's.

lines.tagline: A nut of living steel that shrugs off poison and grows into a heavy-fisted giant.

potent_at.why: The Koga answer. Steel is immune to Poison, and High Horsepower (37) is super effective into Toxtricity and Drapion. Iron Head waits until 36, as Meltan's own first Steel move waits until Flash Cannon at 40 natively, so Meltan does not also sweep Erika (it walls her but cannot break her). The owner's approved 12 moves, re-levelled (owner call: see EXP-049 Results).

lines.tagline: A fragile ember, four times weak to Rock, that repays the wait as a sun moth with Quiver Dance.

potent_at.why: The moth. Bug/Fire is 4x weak to Rock, so it loses Brock outright (the owner accepts it: a Larvesta player catches something for gym 1). From 30 the grown form's Signal Beam (28) and Flamethrower (33) carry Surge and Erika; Volcarona at 45 takes Sabrina with Bug Buzz, and Quiver Dance arrives on that step (the jar's own evolution move) and in the pool at 45. Blaine is its wall. The moves lean special for Volcarona (135 SpA), though the two earlier forms keep Larvesta's physical shape, so Flame Wheel, Bug Bite and Leech Life stay.

lines.tagline: An adaptive and despicable choice of your own fate.

potent_at.why: The painter, played as a fast pivot (the owner, 2026-10-08; docs/research/notes/smeargle-pivot.md): it attacks first for a Protean type, U-turns out, and comes back as something else. Its movepool is what it Sketches. Stages 1 and 2 keep the old 74/79/60/79/60/98 shape at 330 and 430 and only the final takes the pivot spread 92/68/78/68/78/92 at 476 (the owner, 2026-10-08: "old-shape-early"). So built it measured 20/35 against the gym leaders (field 15-20; `python tools/mythical_starters.py measure`, 2026-10-08), the top of the field with Cosmog and Misdreavus, Sketching only the moves of earlier gym leaders' teams, with Gen 9 Protean modelled as one type per duel: 9 at gyms 1-5 and 11 at gyms 6-8. With all three stages in the pivot spread it measured 21/35. The sim models no U-turn switch (battle_sim leaves selfSwitch moves out), so the pivot itself is not in the number. Erika (4/4) and Blaine (4/5) are its best gyms, Surge its weakest (1/4: Magneton only); Giovanni falls to Surf, Moonblast and Thunderbolt (5/6). EXP-065 plays the pivot against Sabrina, Lorelei and Agatha.

tm_additions.decision: The owner, 2026-10-08: Smeargle is a fast pivot (docs/research/notes/smeargle-pivot.md); add U-turn to its TM list so the native TM Machine can teach it from a bug gem without Sketch.
tm_additions.mechanism: Read in the Cobblemon 1.8.0 jar: a `tm:` learnset entry goes into Learnset.tmMoves (the static `tm` interpreter); FormData.getMoves returns the form's own learnset when it sets `moves`; TechnicalMachineItem refuses with tms.cannot_learn unless pokemon.getForm().getMoves().tmLearnableMoves() contains the move, and TechnicalMachine.filterTms filters the machine by the same list. The disc is data/cobblemon/tms/uturn.json (7 bug gems and a Shed Shell, cobblemon:unlockable). Not run in game: EXP-065.

lines.moves_why: Smeargle's 1.8.0 learnset is Sketch at 1 and nine tutor, legacy and special entries (falseswipe, flamethrower, captivate, sleeptalk, furyswipes, meanlook, odorsleuth, seismictoss, spore), read from the jar's generation2/smeargle.json. Seven are spread across the levels: Fury Swipes at 1 so the level-5 starter can attack, False Swipe at 10 for catching, Seismic Toss at 20 (damage equal to its level, whatever its Attack), Mean Look at 27, Flamethrower at 33 (its one strong special move, 79 SpA at 45) and Sleep Talk at 40. Left out on purpose: Spore (the owner, 2026-10-08: Spore and Shell Smash arrive only through Sketch), Captivate and Odor Sleuth (no use here). One TM entry, `tm:uturn` (tm_additions: the owner, 2026-10-08, the fast pivot), so the native TM Machine teaches U-turn without Sketch. Everything else is Sketch's: the movepool is what the player shows it.

lines.tagline: A little ghost that teases its way down the road, until the thing it was haunting steps out of the past: a paradox at full strength from the day it arrives.

potent_at.why: The ghost. Measured 20/35 against the gym leaders (field 15-20; `python tools/mythical_starters.py measure`, 2026-10-08), the top of the field with Cosmog. Confusion and Disarming Voice scrape one win off Brock; Hex and Psybeam take Misty's Horsea and Lombre; Mismagius at 30 carries Koga with Dazzling Gleam and Psybeam (3/5); Flutter Mane at 45 (135 SpA and Speed) takes Sabrina with Shadow Ball and Blaine with Psybeam and Dazzling Gleam (4/5 each). Surge and Erika are its weak gyms. Moonblast and Power Gem were tried in the pool and left out: with them it measured 21/35, above the field. Protosynthesis is not modelled (battle_sim has no such ability), and Flutter Mane learns Sunny Day at 1, which switches it on.

lines.final_why: The owner, 2026-10-08: Misdreavus -> Mismagius -> Flutter Mane, the starter line only. Flutter Mane is not Mismagius's evolution in the jar (Mismagius has `evolutions: []`; Flutter Mane has none and no `preEvolution`), so the 45 step is a CROSS-SPECIES evolution into an unrelated species: an evolution's result is a free PokemonProperties string (jar Evolution.evolutionMethod clones, then getResult().apply(pokemon); Pokemon.setSpecies writes only the species field, then updateAspects, updateForm, checkGender, updateHP and attemptAbilityUpdate). Flutter Mane is `implemented` by COBBLEVERSE-DP-v31 data/cobblemon/species_additions/fluttermane.json, not by the bare jar. Wild Misdreavus and Mismagius carry no starter aspect, so they keep their own (Dusk Stone) evolution and never reach Flutter Mane; and the starter's Misdreavus form never takes a Dusk Stone, because a form's evolutions are its own set or empty, never the species' (jar FormData.getEvolutions: `_evolutions ?: LinkedHashSet()`); paradoxes stay dungeon content everywhere else (docs/STATE.md). Until the AllTheMons models ship (ADR-006) Flutter Mane renders as the placeholder doll.

models_pending.why: The owner, 2026-10-08, chose to ship the AllTheMons models for Flutter Mane; that delivery waits on the licence (docs/decisions/ADR-006-server-delivered-client-pack.md, 'Prepared and verified'). Until it ships, Flutter Mane renders as the placeholder doll in game. tools/player_guide_starters.py says so in the starter page's 'What this page leaves out'; remove a species from this list when its model reaches players.

lines.moves_why: A Ghost/Fairy special set, every move in the 1.8.0 learnset of Misdreavus, Mismagius or Flutter Mane (the jar's generation2/misdreavus.json, generation4/mismagius.json, generation9/fluttermane.json). Astonish and Confusion at 1 (Misdreavus's own) so the level-5 starter can attack; Disarming Voice (Flutter Mane TM) at 10 for Fairy before the final; Confuse Ray at 14; Hex at 21 and Will-O-Wisp at 27 pair (Hex doubles on a burned target), both after Brock's cap of 20; Psybeam at 25; Draining Kiss (Misdreavus TM) at 29; Mystical Fire (Mismagius's level-1 move) at 32, just after the step to Mismagius; Dazzling Gleam at 36 (Flutter Mane's own level 35); Shadow Ball at 41, after Koga's cap of 40; Calm Mind at 43. Left out on purpose: Moonblast (Flutter Mane's level 84) and Power Gem (measured 21/35 with both, above the field), Memento and Perish Song. After 45 Flutter Mane's own learnset takes over: Mystical Fire 49, Power Gem 56, Psyshock 63, Moonblast 84.
